extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, practicing chymists/early chemists, and learned readers interested in experimental philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging chymical (chemical) theories, experiments, and reports — e.g., what counts as convincing experimental evidence, robust explanation, and reliable experimental reporting in the study of substances and 'principles' (elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for personal observation (autopsia)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'little less than [autopsia] seems requisite to make a man sure there _is_.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct inspection/first-hand observation or replication is required to be confident about extraordinary experimental claims (i.e., do not accept stupendous effects on mere hearsay or authority). The author insists on personal verification as a standard for belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory (causal) account beyond mere experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Chymists have been much more happy in finding Experiments than the Causes of them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A satisfactory scientific account must do more than report phenomena; it should aim to explain causes and mechanisms. Experimental reports that lack causal explanation are insufficient for establishing true understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and intelligibility of theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of writers (e.g., Paracelsus) who present 'Phantastick and Un-intelligible Discourses' despite good experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theories should be taught and argued clearly and intelligibly; attractive or showy language is not a substitute for rigorous, comprehensible argumentation. Avoid obscure, fanciful, or needlessly opaque theorizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn constituent parts by particular experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: 'the surest way is to Learn by particular Experiments, what differing parts particular Bodies do consist of...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations of what bodies consist of should be made by careful, targeted experiments on the specific substance in question (not by sweeping deduction). Use experiment to discover constituent parts rather than deducing them from general preconceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely solely on fire for analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice to discern parts 'either Actual or potential fire' but 'without relying too much upon the Fire alone.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical methods should be plural: do not assume that the results of heating/distillation are definitive if those methods can themselves produce artifacts. Complement thermal analysis with other techniques/approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid forcing bodies into arbitrary element-count schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Objection to the certainty of a fixed number of principles/elements (three, five, etc.) and to forcing bodies 'into more Elements than Nature made Them up of.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious of explanatory schemes that rigidly impose a fixed number of 'principles' or 'elements' on nature; allow empirical results to determine how many distinct constituents are warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight given to repeated trials and empirical frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: 'the numerous tryals of those you call the vulgar Chymists, may be allow'd to prove something too.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproducibility and the accumulation of repeated trials are valid evidence; many consistent experiments by practitioners deserve consideration even if their theoretical framing is crude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolate principles for practical/medical investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that 'Divers of the Qualities of a mixt Body, and especially the Medical Virtues, do for the most part lodge in some One or Other of its principles.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fractionation/isolation of components is a useful practical strategy, especially when seeking medicinal properties. Emphasizes practical utility in guiding analytical priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize substances by specific chemical reactivity and sensory tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental characterizations: e.g., the salt 'hisses upon the Affusion of Spirit of Nitre, or Oyle of Vitriol; it precipitates Corals Dissolv'd in Spirit of Vinager; it turnes the blew Syrup of Violets immediately green; it presently turnes the Solution of Sublimate into a Milkie whiteness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, repeatable chemical tests and sensory observations (color changes, precipitations, effervescence, smell, taste) to discriminate and describe substances. Provide the reactions used as diagnostic criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed experimental reporting (materials, proportions, apparatus, procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipes and procedure-level detail: 'Take then of good Antimony, Salt-Petre and Tartar, of each an equal weight, and of Quicklime Halfe the Weight... have in readiness a long neck or Retort of Earth... cast in the above prepar'd Mixture...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good experimental accounts should give materials, weights/proportions, apparatus description, stepwise procedure, heating conditions, and the observable results so that others can reproduce the experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for provenance and co-mixture effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples that source and admixture change results: burying copper plates in grape marc produces verdigrease whose distillate differs; mixing saline with metalline parts alters the distill'd liquor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the source, prior treatments, and co-present materials (metals, husks, marc, etc.) when interpreting results — the same named substance from different contexts may behave differently because of prior associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be skeptical of analytical artifacts produced by the method
rubrics_metrics.description: 'when a Body is resolv'd by the Fire into its suppos'd simple Ingredients, those substances are not true and proper Elements, but rather were, as it were, Accidentally produc'd by the fire'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an analysis method (e.g., destructive heating) generates products, investigators must test whether those products are genuine components of the original substance or artifacts created by the analytical process itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect efficacy of different physical agents (heat and cold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that Heat and Cold both have significant operative effects (e.g., quenching red-hot steel in cold water changes hardness and brittleness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disparage agents that seem 'elementary' or 'insipid' (like cold or water); experiments must consider a variety of physical agents and conditions since they can produce substantial transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual humility and readiness to revise views on rational grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that if rival theories 'shall upon rational and Experimental grounds be clearly made out to me; I shall not be so farr in Love with my Disquieting Doubts, as not to be content to change them for undoubted truths.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain willingness to change one's opinions when clear, rational, experimental evidence warrants it. Scientific judgment values evidence over prior attachment to paradox or hypothesis.
